===BEGIN gaps.json===
{
  "run_id": "a274d1d20c2f",
  "round": 2,
  "topic": "version-aware multimodal evidence provenance and reference grounding across revised workplace attachments, including cross-version region lineage, email-to-attachment referring expressions, workbook-level spreadsheet structure, and hierarchical provenance from attachment version through page, element, region or cell to answer span",
  "gaps": [
    {
      "id": "gap-1",
      "description": "The corpus still does not establish a complete method for maintaining evidence provenance across successive workplace attachment revisions, including stable attachment identity, version-relative source locations, semantic changes between versions, and lineage from an older cited region to its later counterpart. VersionRAG covers explicit version-aware retrieval in technical documentation, and 2607.14117 covers cross-version element alignment in scientific PDFs, but neither validates the complete attachment-revision provenance problem.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"document version alignment\" multimodal provenance region lineage semantic change revised documents",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open. Papers 2510.08109 and 2607.14117 address version-aware retrieval and cross-version element alignment respectively, but the evidence supplied for round 2 does not establish stable workplace-attachment identity, version-relative source coordinates, semantic-change tracking, and cited-region lineage jointly in one validated method."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-2",
      "description": "Direct grounding of workplace-message language such as \"this screenshot\", \"the highlighted row\", or \"numbers below\" into an attachment, cell, page element, or document region remains unvalidated. Scene-text referring-expression comprehension and visually grounded dialogue provide adjacent-domain mechanisms but not email-to-attachment evaluation.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"referring expression grounding\" document multimodal email attachment table cell screenshot coreference",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open. doi-10-1109-tmm-2022-3219642 and doi-10-18653-v1-2025-acl-long-547 provide adjacent evidence for referring-expression or visually grounded language, but no supplied paper evaluates workplace-message-to-attachment grounding for references to screenshots, highlighted rows, tables, cells, or document regions."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-3",
      "description": "Spreadsheet understanding beyond isolated tables remains open. The newer spreadsheet papers cover workbook-level inspection, structure extraction, verification, multi-sheet business workflows, and target-cell modification, but the corpus still does not establish comprehensive treatment of formulas, hidden rows or sheets, cross-sheet references, merged regions, formatting semantics, units, named ranges, and provenance across revised workbook versions.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"spreadsheet understanding\" workbook formulas hidden sheets named ranges merged cells cross-sheet provenance",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open. Papers 2604.12282 and 2606.29955 broaden workbook-level spreadsheet coverage, but the supplied analyses do not establish comprehensive handling of formulas, hidden structures, named ranges, formatting semantics, merged regions, units, cross-sheet dependencies, and provenance across workbook revisions."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-4",
      "description": "No admitted paper validates an end-to-end provenance representation that jointly identifies attachment version, page, document element, exact region or cell, and answer span. Individual studies validate different subsets of this hierarchy, but their combination remains untested.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"evidence provenance\" document question answering page region cell answer span multimodal grounding",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open. The supplied corpus contains mechanisms at different provenance levels in 2607.14117, 2511.12003, manual-0661fc0cba, doi-10-18653-v1-2020-acl-main-398, and 2609.08364, but no supplied paper validates the complete attachment-version-to-page-to-element-to-region-or-cell-to-answer-span hierarchy end to end."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-5",
      "description": "End-to-end behavior when extraction or grounding is unsupported, incomplete, or wrong remains insufficiently exercised. The corpus contains unanswerable-question evaluation and analyses of parser, localization, retrieval, OCR, and grounding failures, but no complete engineering contract distinguishing successful absence from parser, OCR, layout, or grounding failure.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve by defining an explicit typed failure contract and exercising it with fault-injection and golden integration tests. The implementation should distinguish at minimum: evidence genuinely absent, unsupported file or feature, parser failure, OCR failure, layout or structural extraction failure, retrieval miss, grounding ambiguity, grounding mismatch, and downstream answer-generation failure. Build fixtures where each failure is independently induced, require machine-readable status and provenance diagnostics, and verify that unsupported or failed extraction cannot be silently represented as an evidence-negative answer. Existing evidence such as 2407.01523, 2607.24651, 2608.03292, and 2111.07129 can inform test cases, but additional papers are not required to specify or benchmark this contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-6",
      "description": "Robustness of candidate extraction and structural-preservation pipelines on heterogeneous workplace documents remains an engineering gap. Existing studies expose failures involving sparse tables, heterogeneous reading order, OCR dependence, parser coverage, and layout errors, but do not jointly benchmark sparse tables, merged structures, OCR corruption, irregular reading order, embedded images, and scanned pages under one workplace-style test suite.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve by constructing a controlled heterogeneous-document benchmark rather than searching for a new algorithmic contribution. Assemble representative PDFs, office documents, screenshots, scans, and spreadsheets with annotated reading order, table structure, merged cells or regions, embedded images, OCR text, and expected provenance. Add perturbation variants for scan quality, rotation, OCR corruption, sparse tables, irregular layouts, and mixed native-plus-raster content. Measure extraction completeness, structural fidelity, reading-order accuracy, region localization, OCR accuracy where applicable, and provenance retention per parser and pipeline configuration. The failure modes reported by 2111.07129, doi-10-1007-s00521-022-06948-5, 1911.10683, and 2607.24651 can seed the benchmark cases."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-7",
      "description": "Operational scaling remains open for long documents, large tables, and spreadsheet workbooks. Reported methods expose quadratic table-relation inference, page-count memory pressure, information loss under page compression, model input cut-offs or merging, and substantial multi-agent extraction latency.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "MEDIUM",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve with implementation-level scalability benchmarks across controlled document and workbook sizes. Sweep page count, table row and column count, workbook sheet count, formula and dependency count, image count, OCR page fraction, and retrieved-candidate count. Record wall-clock latency, peak memory, CPU or accelerator utilization, token or API consumption where applicable, extraction and grounding accuracy, and degradation caused by truncation, chunking, page compression, or candidate pruning. Profile asymptotic hot paths and compare batching, streaming, hierarchical retrieval, caching, and incremental version processing. The constraints reported in 2111.07129, 2212.05935, 2412.18424, and 2604.12282 provide benchmark targets but do not require additional academic literature to measure the engineering envelope."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-8",
      "description": "The corpus lacks one evaluation that simultaneously scores semantic correctness, extraction completeness, exact provenance, unsupported-evidence handling, and preservation of tables, images, and reading order on workplace-style attachments. Existing benchmarks and metrics cover subsets of these properties rather than the complete combination.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve by defining and implementing a composite workplace-attachment evaluation suite with separately reported dimensions rather than collapsing them into an unsupported single quality score. Create gold annotations for answer semantics, evidence completeness, attachment version, page, element, region or cell, answer span, unanswerable or unsupported cases, table structure, image associations, and reading order. Evaluate exact and tolerant localization, answer correctness, provenance completeness, unsupported-evidence behavior, and structural preservation, then publish per-dimension and end-to-end pass rates. Existing metrics and benchmark practices from doi-10-18653-v1-2025-findings-naacl-295, 2407.01523, 2606.29955, 2111.07129, and doi-10-1007-s00521-022-06948-5 can be combined operationally without requiring another paper to define the test harness."
    }
  ],
  "convergence": {
    "should_continue": true,
    "reason": "open_gaps_remain",
    "next_round_topic": "Cross-version multimodal document grounding: stable region and element lineage across revised attachments, message-to-attachment referring expressions, revised-workbook provenance, and end-to-end hierarchical evidence identifiers from version through page, region or cell to answer span."
  }
}
===END gaps.json===
